title: api: ensure consistent rate-limit semantics and idempotency for streaming + openai-compat
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: Users integrating long-lived streaming requests (chat completions / tool-calling) saw inconsistent 429 and Retry-After behavior between our native API and the OpenAI compatibility layer. In some failure modes streaming handlers dropped partial responses without any idempotency/dedup window, and retry semantics were unclear to SDKs. This PR unifies rate-limit semantics and idempotency guarantees for streaming endpoints and maps them consistently in the OpenAI compatibility shim.

What this does (high level):
- Return Retry-After and consistent X-RateLimit headers for streaming endpoints on 429 and quota errors (both native and openai-compat).
- Add idempotency key support for streaming requests so that retried streams (same idempotency key) are deduplicated on the server side; partial fragments from the first in-progress stream can be replayed when possible.
- Extend error payloads to always include a structured error object with code, message, and type (maps to OpenAI-style error structure for compat layer).
- Update OpenAI compatibility layer mapping so that OpenAI clients receive 429/Retry-After semantics they expect and error codes are translated predictably.
- Add integration tests for streaming idempotency and retry-after behavior, update docs and SDK compatibility shim.

Checklist: [x] Add server-side Retry-After header for streaming 429s; [x] Implement streaming idempotency key handler and storage TTL; [x] Map internal error codes to openai-compat error schema; [x] Add integration tests; [x] Docs: rate limit docs + examples; [x] Add SDK compatibility change for Python/TS.

Notes and rationale: Idempotency for streaming is tricky because streams may emit partial events before the server finalizes the response. We adopt a best-effort replay approach: the first successful stream writes a small replay log (up to N bytes/chunks) for the idempotency window (configurable, default 5m). A retried request with the same key within the window will be served from the replay log when possible. This avoids lost responses during transient network errors while bounding storage and complexity. The approach is documented and opt-in via idempotency-key header for now.

Related Linear: [ENG-2345], [ENG-2768].

review_comments: Ava Thompson: Left a couple nits on header naming — prefer 'Retry-After' + 'X-RateLimit-Reset' for consistency with infra metrics. Also: add a small proof that replay size bounds are enforced to avoid memory growth.
Author (Sofia Martinez): Addressed naming nits and added a replay_size_limit check in idempotency.rs + unit test to assert eviction under heavy chunking.

Marco Lee: Question about failure modes — what happens if the first stream partially wrote to the replay log but the process crashes before marking it final? Suggest write-ahead marker to avoid serving incomplete replays.
Author: Added a write-ahead marker and a short grace window to avoid serving incomplete logs; documented behavior in comments and docs.
release_notes: Unifies rate limit semantics across streaming and OpenAI-compat endpoints. Adds optional idempotency-key support for streaming requests to deduplicate retries and offers Retry-After headers on 429 responses. Backwards-compatible: idempotency is opt-in and default behavior unchanged unless header provided.
testing_notes: Integration harness reproduces race between partial stream writes and retries; tests assert that retried requests with same idempotency-key either replay partial output or are rejected with 409 if key already consumed. Added load test for header throughput to ensure no measurable latency regression.
deploy_notes: Feature gated behind config 'streaming_idempotency_enabled' (default true for canary). OpenAI compat mapping toggled by 'openai_compat_retry_after' flag. Recommend canary rollout to dedicated clusters first and monitor rate-limit/metering dashboards for unexpected traffic spikes.
